questions.note: Order reads right at native size: the hallux is longest, toe 2 a little shorter, toes 3–4 descending. Individual shaping is weak: toe 2 is an even tube; from below both pads are thimbles and toe 2 is stacked cylinders with ledged creases; in profile the IP crease is a hard notch; the knuckle wrinkles are one stamp on both toes.

The corner tears are gone and the free edge has thickness, but both nails read as press-ons: rounded-rectangle tiles in a constant-width channel, nearly flat, root exposed as a white lip, one milky tone with no lunula or pink bed, an opaque French tip with a wavy bead, combed streaks in every highlight. Not trimmed straight.

No extensor relief reads in these frames: no EHL cord over the first MTP or along the hallux, no slip to toe 2, no dorsal veins; the only linear relief on the MTP dorsum is a glossy, scar-like line. The saphenous vein lies outside these frames, so it is not judged.

SSS is controlled: shadow sides stay dark, no glow. The micro-relief fails: a uniform outlined-cell crackle at about twice the spec's cell size on every surface, straight corduroy ridges on the pads, no visible pits. The declared first-pass material's wet sheen over one even pink is not scored, though it makes the toes read as silicone.

defects.what: The hallux plate sits in a constant-width groove with a raised rim tracing its whole outline, and its proximal edge is exposed as a crisp lip: an inset panel. No proximal fold rolls over the root; toe 2's nail repeats the same template.
defects.fix: Let the proximal fold roll over the root so the plate emerges from under the eponychium, and let the lateral folds rise softly and overlap the plate's edges unevenly, fading out toward the free edge.

defects.what: The hallux plate is nearly flat side to side: its lateral thirds do not curve down into the folds, so it reads as a flat tile rather than a shell with an 11 mm transverse radius.
defects.fix: Curve the plate transversely to the spec radius (11 mm hallux, 6 mm toe 2) so its sides fall into the lateral grooves and the highlight wraps across it.

defects.what: The hallux plate is one milky pink-grey from root to free edge: no lunula crescent at the root, no pink bed seen through a clear plate, no paler onychodermal band; it reads as frosted acrylic.
defects.fix: A clear plate (high transmission) over a pink bed, a pale 3.5 mm lunula crescent emerging from under the fold, and a slightly paler band at the onychodermal line before the free edge.

defects.what: The free edge is an opaque grey-white band of even width with a rolled, rubbery bead and a wavy S-shaped outline, like a French manicure; toe 2's is the same.
defects.fix: A trimmed edge is cut straight across with slightly rounded corners: a thin, translucent off-white lip with a flat cut face, slightly irregular, with the hyponychium's shadow beneath.

defects.what: Toe 2's plate (and the hallux's) is combed with bold white longitudinal streaks in every highlight, like brushed metal or anisotropic plastic.
defects.fix: Ridges 0.01 mm deep at 0.25 mm pitch show only as a faint ripple at the edge of a highlight; cut the ridge bump strength and break it up.

defects.what: The skin micro-relief is a Voronoi crackle of dark-outlined polygon cells about 0.4–0.8 mm, equally sharp and deep everywhere and continuing into the folds: crazed glaze or snake skin, visible on every surface at native size.
defects.fix: Toe skin has a finer (0.25–0.4 mm) network of shallow furrows with dominant directions and varying depth, with follicle pits and no outlined cells; soften it in the folds and on the pulps.

defects.what: Plantar friction ridges are straight parallel diagonal stripes at one angle over the ball, the hallux pad and toe 2's pad, running straight through the flexion creases like corduroy.
defects.fix: Ridges form whorls or loops centred on each pulp, follow the pad's contour, and change direction and break at each flexion crease.

defects.what: From below the hallux pulp is a thimble: straight parallel sides, a crisp corner where it meets the IP crease, and a flat face.
defects.fix: A real pulp is an oval, fleshy dome, widest mid-pad, bulging past the toe's sides and rounding smoothly into the IP crease.

defects.what: Toe 2 from below reads as stacked cylinders: a glossy-lipped base groove, then a straight PIP ledge across the whole toe where the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff, with a jagged white fleck at its lateral end.
defects.fix: Flexion creases are soft folds that follow the pad's curvature, deepest mid-toe and fading at the sides, with flesh bulging on both sides and no step in the outline.

defects.what: The 1–2 web's margin is a straight, hard horizontal edge about 7 mm long meeting toe 2's medial wall at a right angle: a flat shelf jutting between the toes.
defects.fix: The web is a soft U-shaped saddle set back between the toes, its margin curving up into each toe's side and shading into the cleft.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are the same stamp: 3–4 smooth, parallel, evenly spaced grooves with glossy lips, corrugating both silhouettes in profile like bellows.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin carries a loose cluster of fine, uneven, partly branching wrinkles of varying length and depth, centred on the joint and fading at the sides, different on each toe.

defects.what: Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is a single long, even groove with a bright lip across the toe: a knife cut.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, shallow creases, broken and uneven, fading out at the sides.

defects.what: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum and nicks the dorsal silhouette in the medial view; it reads as a healed incision.
defects.fix: Skin over the first MTP is smooth or carries a few short, soft wrinkles that fade out; no continuous raised line.

defects.what: In profile the plantar outline under the hallux is pinched into a deep V-notch with a hard lip at the IP crease, so the distal toe reads as a tube plugged into the foot.
defects.fix: The IP flexion crease is a soft dimple between two fleshy pads; the outline dips gently and the skin folds without a lip.

defects.what: Toe 2 is an even-width tube from the PIP knuckle to the pulp, straight-sided, with no PIP swelling and no waist over the middle phalanx.
defects.fix: Swell the PIP condyles, narrow the toe over the middle phalanx and widen it again into the pulp, so the outline undulates.

defects.what: A short red-brown cut runs from the hallux nail's medial distal corner down into the pulp (also at the lateral corner and at toe 2's corners): a pinch where the nail groove ends.
defects.fix: The lateral nail groove fades out at the hyponychium; the pulp below each corner is smooth.

defects.what: From below the hallux free edge's corners show past the pulp's outline as jagged, glassy white shards.
defects.fix: Where the free edge shows past the pulp it is a thin, smooth, translucent rim.

defects.what: From below the hallux has no base crease: its proximal phalanx flows straight into the ball while toe 2 has one, so the big toe reads as a column growing out of the sole.
defects.fix: A deep, curved fold separates the hallux's base from the ball under the first MTP, with flesh bulging on both sides of it.

defects.what: No extensor relief reads: no EHL cord over the first MTP and along the hallux's proximal phalanx, no slip running to toe 2, and no dorsal veins in frame.
defects.fix: The EHL stands as a cord about 1 mm proud from the first metatarsal over the MTP onto the hallux, a slip runs to toe 2, and dorsal veins show as soft 0.7 mm relief catching the rim light.

ranked: [D1] Both nails read as press-ons, one template scaled: a rounded-rectangle tile sunk in a constant-width channel with a raised rim all round and the root exposed as a white lip. A real plate slides out from under a soft proximal fold and tucks under uneven lateral folds.

[D4] The free edges are opaque cream French tips of even width with a rolled, rubbery bead and a wavy S outline; a trimmed toenail ends in a thin, translucent off-white lip cut straight across with slightly rounded corners.

[D3] The hallux plate is one milky pink-grey from root to edge: no lunula, no pink bed seen through a clear plate, no paler band at the onychodermal line, so it reads as frosted acrylic rather than keratin over living tissue.

[D6] Every skin surface wears the same Voronoi crackle: dark-outlined cells about 0.4–0.8 mm, equally sharp and deep everywhere and running into the folds, like crazed glaze or snake skin. Real toe skin has a finer, softer furrow network with direction, varying depth and pores.

[D2] The plates are nearly flat side to side; their lateral thirds do not fall away into the folds. An 11 mm transverse radius (6 mm on toe 2) gives a clearly domed shell whose highlight wraps across it.
[D5] Every nail highlight is combed into bold white longitudinal streaks, like brushed metal, strongest on toe 2; real ridging shows only as a faint ripple at the edge of the highlight.

[D11] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: 3–4 smooth, parallel, evenly spaced grooves with glossy lips that corrugate both silhouettes like bellows. Real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine wrinkles, different on each toe.

[D10] The 1–2 web's margin is a straight, hard horizontal edge about 7 mm long meeting toe 2's wall at a right angle, a shelf between the toes; a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle that curves up into both toes' sides.

The declared first-pass skin material distorts the read in scope: a broad, wet, lacquer-like sheen over one even salmon-pink (no redder knuckles or tip, no darker crease floors) makes both toes read as silicone.

[D7] From below, the friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball and both pads, running straight through the creases like corduroy; pulps carry whorls or loops that follow the pad and break at each crease.
[D8] From below, the hallux pulp is a thimble: straight parallel sides, a crisp corner at the IP crease and a flat face. A real pulp is an oval, fleshy dome, widest mid-pad.

[D9] Toe 2 from below is three stacked cylinders: a glossy-lipped base groove, then a straight PIP ledge where the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff, with a jagged white fleck at its lateral end.
[D15] Toe 2 is an even tube from knuckle to pulp, straight-sided, with no PIP swelling and no waist over the middle phalanx; it reads as a sausage toe with rings.
[D14] In profile the IP crease under the hallux is a deep V-notch with a hard lip, as if the distal toe were a tube plugged into the foot; real skin there dips softly between two fleshy pads.
[D13] A thin, raised, glossy arc across the first MTP dorsum reads as a healed incision, and it nicks the dorsal silhouette in the medial view.
[D19] No extensor relief reads on either toe: no EHL cord over the first MTP and the proximal phalanx, no slip running to toe 2, and no dorsal veins anywhere in frame, so the forefoot looks cast.
[D12] Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip, a knife cut rather than two or three short, soft, broken creases.
[D18] From below, the hallux has no base crease: its proximal phalanx flows straight into the ball while toe 2 has one, so the big toe reads as a column growing out of the sole.
In profile the hallux still reads long and low: its dorsal line is one straight slope from the MTP to the free edge, with no rise over the IP joint or the distal phalanx under the nail.

Both toes are bald: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and no hairs on toe 2 (hair is outside this round's questions, but bald, spotless toes read as a mannequin); the few tiny white flecks on the skin read as lint.
[D16] A short red-brown cut runs from each distal nail corner down into the pulp (clearest at the hallux's medial corner, also on toe 2), a pinch where the nail groove should simply fade out.
[D17] From below, the hallux free edge's corners show past the pulp as jagged, glassy shards.
